Chapter 2. The Endless Work of Maintenance and the Rituals of Womanhood.
As the years go by, those little routines you might've once skipped without a second thought—like smoothing on moisturizer, brushing out your hair, or even touching up your nails—suddenly become non-negotiable. What started as something casual turns into a full-time job. And if you’re nodding along right now, you know exactly what I mean: the effort just to keep up grows, and so does that mix of camaraderie and, honestly, exhaustion among everyone who shares this burden.
But there’s comfort in these rituals, isn’t there? The familiar scent of your favorite lotion, the calming rhythm of brushing your hair, the quiet satisfaction of freshly painted nails—these tiny acts turn into anchors when everything else feels like it’s shifting around you. For a lot of women, the bathroom isn’t just a bathroom anymore. It becomes a kind of sanctuary, a place where the world’s demands and noise just fall away, even if it’s only for a few minutes.
Of course, the sheer volume of maintenance can get overwhelming. Imagine opening your calendar and realizing it’s jam-packed—not with dinners out or fun weekends, but with haircuts, waxing appointments, dental cleanings. One woman laughed when she saw this, but let’s be real—it’s also a little sobering. What once felt like a treat now just looks like an endless to-do list.
And it’s not just your time these rituals demand. There’s the cost, too. The beauty industry knows exactly how to tap into our insecurities about getting older, offering product after product, treatment after treatment—always promising to fix that next little “flaw.” It’s relentless. Sometimes, the bravest thing you can do is just step off the treadmill and say, “Enough.”
Still, there’s pride in all this effort. Keeping up your appearance is more than just vanity—it’s a way of taking charge in a world that can feel chaotic. It’s a statement: “I still matter to myself.” These rituals become a kind of self-respect, a way of honoring your body and everything it’s been through.
And when you’re with friends, maintenance turns into a favorite topic. You swap stories about the latest trends, the best salons, the products that actually deliver. There’s a sense of shared struggle—a recognition that everyone’s fighting the same fight. Laughter breaks through the frustration, and suddenly, even the most annoying parts of upkeep become moments of connection.
But here’s the thing—these rituals aren’t just about looking good. They’re about who you are. They offer a thread of continuity, helping you hold onto the person you’ve always been, even as the years bring change. That comfort in the familiar, it’s a reminder that some things stay constant, no matter what else shifts around you.
At the same time, there’s this growing sense that the whole thing is a little bit absurd. The endless cycle—plucking, dyeing, moisturizing—can start to feel like a performance you never actually signed up for, choreographed by someone else’s expectations. Sometimes, there’s a real temptation to just let go, to choose comfort over keeping up appearances, and embrace the freedom that comes with age.
The journey through maintenance is personal. For some, it’s a joy; for others, it’s a heavy lift. But for everyone, it’s a reminder of just how complicated the relationship is between self-care and self-acceptance. The routines might shift, but that desire to feel good in your own skin? That never really changes.
